string-array.item: Description:\nThe Betta fish (Betta splendens), known as the "Siamese fighting fish", is a freshwater fish famous for its intense colors and long ornamental fins. Originating from Southeast Asia, it belongs to the Osphronemidae family and has an organ called a labyrinth that allows it to breathe oxygen directly from the air. Males are territorial and can display aggressive behaviors towards other bettas, so they are often kept alone in aquariums. Its average size is 6 to 7 cm and its life expectancy ranges from 2 to 5 years. It is an omnivorous fish that feeds on insects, larvae, and commercial food. Reproduction is oviparous, and the male builds bubble nests to protect the eggs. Thanks to its beauty and resilience, it is one of the most popular fish in the global aquarium trade.

Description:\nThe Guppy fish (Poecilia reticulata) is one of the most popular freshwater fish in the aquarium hobby due to its resilience, ease of care, and vibrant colors. Originating from South America, it belongs to the Poeciliidae family and reaches between 2 and 6 cm in length. It is characterized by its striking caudal fin and extraordinary reproductive capacity, as females can give birth to live young several times a year. Its diet is omnivorous, consuming algae, small invertebrates, and commercial food. It has a life expectancy of 1 to 3 years and adapts well to community aquariums, making it ideal for beginners. In addition, its genetic diversity has allowed for the creation of numerous varieties with unique patterns and colors.

Description:\nThe Molly fish (Poecilia sphenops) is one of the most popular species in the aquarium hobby for its resilience and ease of care. Native to Central and South America, it belongs to the Poeciliidae family and is characterized by being ovoviviparous, meaning the young are born live after developing inside the mother. Its average size ranges between 6 and 10 cm, with color varieties such as black, white, orange, and dalmatian. They are peaceful and social fish, ideal for community aquariums, although they require well-oxygenated water with stable parameters. Their diet is omnivorous, based on algae, small invertebrates, and commercial food. With a life expectancy of 3 to 5 years, mollies are known for their adaptability, even in slightly brackish water, making them a versatile option for hobbyists and beginners.
